extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR grobcov.lib (computational algebraists / researchers using comprehensive Groebner systems and locus/envelope computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the grobcov.lib SINGULAR library routines: preconditions, calling conventions, return formats, options, and semantics for computing Comprehensive Groebner Systems, constructible/locu s representations, and related geometric constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: cgsdr (compute disjoint, reduced CGS)
rubrics_metrics.description: cgsdr(ideal F) — F: ideal in Q[a][x] (a = parameters, x = variables). Computes a disjoint, reduced Comprehensive Groebner System (CGS). The basering R must be of the form Q[a][x] and defined previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a list T describing a reduced and disjoint CGS: a list of (full,hole,basis) where ideals full and hole represent the segment V(full) \ V(hole). With option ("out",0) segments are grouped by leading power products (lpp) and given in P-representation. The returned list structure can be either nested lpp-grouped form or [[E,N,B],..] depending on options. Options: "can",0-1-2 (homogenization/canonical choices) — when called directly default is "can",2 (no homogenization); inside grobcov default is "can",1. "null",ideal E (default ("null",ideal(0))). "nonnull",ideal N (default ("nonnull",ideal(1))). "comment",0-1 (default 0). "out",0-1 (default 1): with "out",0 output segments are P-representation grouped by lpp. Note: grobcov uses different specific options internally; when grobcov is computed cgsdr may be invoked with more expensive options. Algorithm used (by default when called directly): Kapur–Sun–Wang algorithm (ISSAC 2010) — efficient but used as starting point for grobcov. Example calls and sample output are shown in the documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: pdivi (pseudodivision by ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: pdivi(poly f, ideal F) — pseudodivision of polynomial f by ideal F in Q[a][x].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs: poly f in Q[a][x]; ideal F divisor in Q[a][x]. Returns a list (poly r, ideal q, poly m) where r is the remainder of pseudodivision, q is the set of quotients, and m is the coefficient factor so that m*f = r + sum(q_i * F_i). Guarantee: no lpp of a divisor divides a pp of r. Example usage shown and verified via r[3]*f - (sum) = 0 in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: pnormalf (reduction modulo a segment)
rubrics_metrics.description: pnormalf(poly f, ideal E, ideal N) — reduce polynomial f modulo V(E) \ V(N) of a segment in Q[a].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a reduced polynomial g of f whose coefficients are reduced modulo E and having no factor in N. Notes: Should be called from ring Q[a][x]. Ideals E and N must be given by polynomials in Q[a]. Example provided demonstrating reduction when p=c-1 and q=a-b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crep (canonical C-representation of locally closed set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crep(ideal N, ideal M) — canonical C-representation [P,Q] of the locally closed set V(N) \ V(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs: ideals N (null ideal) and M (hole ideal) in Q[a] (parameters only). Returns a pair of radical ideals [P,Q] with P included in Q representing V(P) \ V(Q) = V(N) \ V(M). Can be called in ring Q[a][x] or Q[a]. Example mapping given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prep (canonical P-representation of locally closed set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prep(ideal N, ideal M) — canonical P-representation of the locally closed set V(N) \ V(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs: ideals N and M in Q[a]. Output: [Comp1, .. , Comps] where each Comp_i = [p_i, [p_i1,..,p_is_i]] giving the P-representation components. To be called in ring Q[a][x] or Q[a]. Examples show resulting components and how they list factors/polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: PtoCrep (convert P-representation to C-representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: PtoCrep(list L) — converts a P-representation list L = [Comp1,..,Comps] (P-representation of V(N) \ V(M)) to the canonical C-representation [P,Q].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input L must be P-representation (list of Comp_i = [p_i,[p_i1,..]]). Returns canonical C-representation [P,Q] (pair of radical ideals P included in Q). Examples illustrate usage and outputs. Call in ring Q[a][x] or Q[a], ideals contain only parameters in Q[a].

rubrics_metrics.name: extendpoly (extend I-regular function representation on a segment)
rubrics_metrics.description: extendGC/extendpoly: extendGC(poly f, ideal p, ideal q) / extendpoly(f,p,q) — extend generic representation of an I-regular function F defined on segment S = V(p) \ V(q) to a full representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs: f is polynomial in Q[a][x] in generic representation of an I-regular function on S. p,q are ideals in Q[a] (Crep of segment S). Basering must be Q[a][x]. Return: an extended representation of F in S; can be a single polynomial or a set of polynomials when needed (one polynomial may vanish at some points but full rep consists of representatives so at least one specializes non-zero). Examples show how extendpoly returns alternate polynomial representatives for different components.

rubrics_metrics.name: extendGC (compute full representation of grobcov output)
rubrics_metrics.description: extendGC(list GC) — given grobcov output computed with option "rep",2, compute the full representation of bases (full representation of I-regular functions forming the bases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: GC must be grobcov of a parametric ideal computed with option "rep",2. extendGC returns structure of the form [[[lpp1,basis1,segment1,lpph1],...,[lpps,basiss,segments,lpphs]]] where each function of the basis can be given by an ideal of representatives. Basering must be Q[a][x]. Note: computing full representation directly via grobcov with option "ext",1 is possible but more time-consuming; alternatively compute grobcov with default ext and rep,2 and call extendGC afterwards. Examples show typical returned nested lists and how representatives are arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConsLevels (canonical closures of constructible set levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: ConsLevels(list L) — given L = [[P1,Q1],...,[Ps,Qs]] (Crep components) representing constructible set S = union V(Pi) \ V(Qi), compute closures of canonical levels of S and its complement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list of ideals [a1,a2,...,at] representing closures of the canonical levels of S and C (complement) wrt closure of S. The canonical levels of S are represented by their Crep; Levels can be obtained by calling Levels on the output. Note: algorithm described in J.M. Brunat & A. Montes (2016). Example demonstrates call sequence Crep->list L->ConsLevels->Levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels (select levels from ConsLevels output)
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels(list L) — given output L = [a1,a2,..,ak] from ConsLevels, select the levels of the constructible set S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns Lc = [[1,[a1,a2]],[3,[a3,a4]],..] — the list of levels of S. To be called in ring Q[a][x] or Q[a]. Example shows constructing P/Q pairs and obtaining levels via ConsLevels then Levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: locus (compute locus taxonomy and components)
rubrics_metrics.description: locus(ideal F[,options]) — determine the locus of points of a geometric construction defined by the input ideal F (system equations). The input ring must be parametric in Q[x1..xn][u1..um] with tracer variables x (space of dimension n) and mover variables u (the last m variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: "grobcov", list (previously computed grobcov(F)) to reuse; "anti-image",0 to suppress anti-image for "Normal" components; "comments", c (0 default). Return: list of components ((p1,(p11,..),tax1),..,(pk,(pk1..),takk)) where element 1&2 are P-canonical form, element 3 tax is: for normal point components tax=(d,taxonomy,anti-image) with taxonomy "Normal" or "Special" and anti-image ideal over mover variables; for non-normal components tax=(d,taxonomy) with taxonomy "Accumulation" or "Degenerate". Definitions: Normal component — each point has 0-dimensional anti-image and anti-image dimension equals component dimension; Special — each point 0-dim anti-image but anti-image in mover coords smaller than component dimension; Accumulation — points have anti-image dimension >0 and component dim < n-1; Degenerate — anti-image dimension >0 and component dim = n-1. Note: if a normal point component has degree > 9 taxonomy may not be determined; returns (n,'normal',0) where n = space dimension. Uses Groebner Cover methodology and references. Example provided with Concoid showing Normal/Special components and returned polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: locusdg (filter Dynamic Geometry relevant components)
rubrics_metrics.description: locusdg(list L) — calling sequence locusdg(locus(S)). Returns the list of "Relevant" components for Dynamic Geometry computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is list of relevant components C_i = [p_i,[p_i1,..], "Relevant", level_i]. "Relevant" components are the "Normal" and "Accumulation" components of the locus (see locus help). Example demonstrates extracting relevant components from locus output.

rubrics_metrics.name: envelop (compute envelope of a family of hypersurfaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: envelop(poly F, ideal C[,options]) — compute the envelope of a family of hypersurfaces represented by polynomial F(x,u) with restrictions ideal C on the parameter variables. The ring convention: ring R=(0,x1,..,xn),(u1,..,um),lp; s < m where s = number of polynomials in C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: F(x1..xn,u1..um) family of hypersurfaces; ideal C = {g1(u),..,gs(u)} restrictions on parameters. Internally calls grobcov and locus. Returns list of components [C1,..,Cn] where each Ci = [pi,[pi1,..,pi_s_i],tax] with canonical P-representation and tax following locus conventions (for normal-point components tax=[d,taxonomy,anti-image], for non-normal-point components tax=[d,taxonomy]). Options: "comments", c (default 0) and "anti-image", a (default 1 show anti-image for Normal components; a=0 hides it). Basering must be Q[x][u]. Uses generalized envelope definition from A. Montes. Examples and usage notes are provided.
